categories.directive: Performance work. Before changing anything, measure with a command you can rerun, and keep its output. After the change, rerun the same command on the same input. Report both numbers and the command. Make no speed or memory claim without both measurements.

kit.directive: Performance work. Read "{playbook}" first. Before changing anything, time the command on a fixed input: python3 "{tool}" run --out-dir <scratchpad>/perf --name before --input <input id> -- <command>. After the change, run the same with --name after, then python3 "{tool}" compare on the two records. Report its verdict, both medians and the command. Make no speed or memory claim without both records.

categories.directive: Visual work. After producing output, render it to an image and look at the image before reporting. If a reference image or mockup was given, compare against it and say what differs. Do not describe how the output looks from the code alone.

categories.directive: Scientific or numerical work, where recalled domain facts are often wrong. Start your reply with one bold line saying this is domain work you will ground before coding. Then: look in the project reference ({reference}) for a relevant entry. If there is none, read primary sources first and add an entry with its source. Validate the code against a case with a known answer, and state units for every quantity.

kit.directive: Scientific or numerical work, where recalled domain facts are often wrong. Start your reply with one bold line saying this is domain work you will ground before coding. Read "{playbook}". Look in the project reference ({reference}) for a relevant entry; if there is none, read primary sources first and add an entry with its source. Record each check of a result against an independent expectation with python3 "{tool}" add --record <scratchpad>/validation.jsonl, and run its summary before reporting. State units for every quantity.

categories.directive: Multi-step work. Write the steps as a Markdown checklist to plan.md in your scratchpad directory before starting, and tick each item when it is done. In the final report, account for every item: done, deferred with the reason, or dropped with the reason.

categories.directive: Work for a reader (a course, lessons, tutorial, guide, documentation, long report or explanation). Before building all of it: (1) state in one or two lines which reading of the request's key phrase you are taking, and who the reader is and what they are assumed to know, in the user's own words where they gave them; (2) build one representative piece first (one lesson, one section) and show it to the user before producing the rest; (3) if the user stated a level or goal, check that piece's order, pitch and wording against it before showing it. For a short answer, skip step 2.

_note: In a directive, {reference} is replaced by how to search the project reference: the check_reference.py the hook finds beside itself or in ../reference-store/, else docs/reference/INDEX.md. A category's optional kit directive replaces its directive when grounding-kits/<dir>/ with the named tool and playbook is found beside the hook or one level up; {tool} and {playbook} become their absolute paths.
